native_member_interfaces.ESS-002: The actual loss-linked hazardous state, exposure and causal assumptions are represented using these process observations/predictions or control actions; the hazard is not equated with a failed component or a natural-process limit.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-003: An actual enforced constraint uses this monitored/predicted state or adjustment; its required bound, actor and feedback delimit the quantitative decision.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-005: A represented function/item failure mode actually uses the quantitative condition, probability or detection/adjustment policy in FMEA/FMECA; evidence remains conditional on that exact failure definition, exposure and detection role, never completeness of FMEA.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-006: A defined top event or post-initiator branch actually consumes this quantitative condition, regime, adjustment mechanism or detector delay; the causal logic defines the event and dependence question rather than being inferred from a signal.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-007: A real process node/deviation uses the stated limit, forecast, detection or adjustment condition; the node, consequence and response specify what deviation matters. A guideword alone supplies no calibrated distribution.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-008: The actual controller/process/context contains this monitoring or adjustment policy; the quantitative conditions expose a possible unsafe action/context and the scenario specifies the relevant statistical consequence.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-009: The same feedback/control path consumes the actual statistical state or policy; achieved-state evidence, freshness and fallback conditions remain separate requirements.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-010: An actual safety process-model/mode assumption consumes the forecast or monitor result and changes after adjustment; its scope, divergence and fail-bounded use define the quantitative target.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-011: The actual control path has timing, order, duration, repetition and transition requirements; the statistic's horizon and intervention cadence must match them and its uncertainty cannot create a deadline waiver.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-012: A specific interface contract relies on a statistical regime, detection property, margin or adjustment assumption; the version-bound assumption identifies the actual cross-boundary quantitative consumer.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-013: The actual common-cause claim involves shared monitored streams, regimes or adjustment resources; those dependencies and observation requirements bound the credited statistical/evidence contribution without manufacturing independence.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-014: A real redundancy architecture uses the quantitative failure/health or adjustment policy and its arbitration/maintenance work; actual dependencies and degraded-mode duties specify the needed statistical claim.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-015: A selected quantitative monitor/forecast or adjustment-mechanism analysis is proposed to cover a named causal question in the actual method portfolio; its supported and omitted phenomena determine contribution, not method count.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-016: The actual human-automation safety role receives the quantitative cue or adjustment work; realistic joint capability, state visibility, takeover and fallback authority bound its use.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-017: A named enforcement actor is credited with using this information and doing its resulting work; the actual competence/information/stop/handoff requirements constrain the policy while no statistical result grants rights.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-018: This quantitative evidence item is actually linked to a hazard/constraint/control claim; its precise condition and supported scope determine what the link can assert, and that hazard-linked target supplies the evidence consumer.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-019: The actual risk representation uses this process evidence or adjustment consequence; consequence, exposure and uncertainty remain separate, and no score or typical band substitutes for the risk claim.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-020: The actual choice of control strength consumes predicted observability/recovery, quantitative margin or monitor/adjustment burden; real consequence, coupling, reversibility and latency delimit its proportionality calculation.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-021: The residual-risk decision actually consumes this quantitative evidence and policy alternatives; its exposure/configuration/time scope and competent authority constrain the offered claim without being supplied by arithmetic.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-022: A real feasible-control comparison uses this detection/forecast/adjustment evidence and total sacrifice; binding good practice and actual consequence remain constraints, and no imported numerical rule creates legal acceptability.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-023: An actual barrier layer has the monitored health, future availability or adjustment process at issue; distinct barrier functions, common causes and escalation duties identify what the statistic must support.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-024: A specified safety function's integrity/assurance argument actually uses this quantitative evidence or monitor; hazard-derived function/exposure and domain objectives delimit that contribution, never a numerical certificate of total safety.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-025: A chosen quantitative evidence channel is credited with detecting a named error/failure; its exact discrimination and regime scope bound its information, while the actual assurance target/dependence claim sets its consumer.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-026: The actual assurance argument uses this specific quantitative premise or adjustment result; its supported meaning, uncertainty and decision scope change the argument, whose claim specifies the relevant statistical target.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-027: A real defeater concerns this stream, forecast, index or intervention premise; its exact counterevidence and closure criterion delimit what the statistical result could resolve, not a generic demand for another review.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-028: The reused evidence is this actual statistical result/policy under a stated configuration and environment; regime/meaning changes affect reuse and the identified actual configuration determines the statistical population.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-029: A concrete change affects this quantitative premise, monitor or adjustment policy; regime and intervention effects delimit the affected frontier while the hazard/control dependency defines what needs reassessment.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-030: The actual live assurance claim relies on this monitored/predicted premise; its useful time horizon, change trigger and response burden delimit the statistical procedure.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-031: A scoped independent assessment actually uses this quantitative check to expose a particular failure; discrimination and limits bound its credit while the assessor's real question and access constrain what can be concluded.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-032: The actual selected quantitative evidence supports a precise hazard-linked model/system claim; the claim's bearer and correspondence burden constrain its target, and statistical evidence never converts a model theorem into a physical guarantee.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-033: The actual monitoring/adjustment policy shares a safety-security feedback, access or availability path; its change/response consequences enter that common path and the named threat/control constraint bounds the policy.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-034: A real hazard detector routes an actionable response from this stream or forecast; its false/missed/late behavior and total alarm burden enter the specific control path.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-035: The actual containment/isolation/stop decision uses the quantitative condition or adjustment; resulting state, actuation and side effects remain separate, and the required controlled state supplies the statistical criterion.
native_member_interfaces.ESS-036: A real continued-service/degradation choice uses the performance forecast or monitor/adjustment policy; competing service loss and credible fallback specify its target and constraints.

record.name: Physical result/reference input to CSS-L1

ECSE-01.native_component: The documented external-reference dependency of a physical result actually used by the coupled work arrangement.

ECSE-02.directional_reason: Reference-comparable physical values can change whether a modeled resource constraint is actually met; they do not choose purposes or validate the whole hierarchy.
ECSE-02.native_component: Physical process/resource values in the checked means–ends constraint model.

ECSE-03.directional_reason: The result's reference, units and uncertainty prevent a stored/transformed value from acquiring a false comparable meaning; memory support still depends on actual use.
ECSE-03.native_component: An actual physical measurement result preserved or transformed by the external representation.

ECSE-04.directional_reason: Comparable duration or physical performance results can change the capability comparison used by coordination design, without making the allocation or coordination feasible by themselves.
ECSE-04.native_component: Measured physical task-capability or timing comparisons used in allocation and recovery design.

ECSE-05.native_component: An actual measured transition duration or physical capacity component used to judge the feasibility of changing the assignment.

ECSE-06.directional_reason: A comparable elapsed-time component can change the burden left or displaced across roles, without measuring subjective effort or proving adequate staffing.
ECSE-06.native_component: Whole-cycle task durations and prolonged automated-operation exposure in the residual-burden account.

ECSE-07.directional_reason: A reference-corrected state or duration can change the represented action-relevant distinction; a correct number does not demonstrate interpretation in time.
ECSE-07.native_component: A physical state value or physical response window actually represented for the actor's choice.

ECSE-08.directional_reason: Comparable elapsed time changes whether a pending action is still cancellable or already outside its intervention window; no extra status ceremony follows.
ECSE-08.native_component: Elapsed delay or expiry on the native contingent command path, when a time value affects cancellation or commitment.

ECSE-10.directional_reason: A calibrated effect value or duration can distinguish commanded completion from achieved process state; calibration does not add an actuator or independent sensor.
ECSE-10.native_component: Observed physical world effect and measured latency after a consequential command.

ECSE-11.directional_reason: Comparable observations and elapsed time can invalidate a falsely feasible intervention credit; they do not confer rights, competence or resources.
ECSE-11.native_component: Relevant physical observations and the real intervention deadline in the credited protective role.

ECSE-12.directional_reason: A correctly referenced time or outcome changes the evidence for actual correction capability even when the approval click is unchanged.
ECSE-12.native_component: Physical outcome or complete detection-to-recovery time used in testing oversight capability.

ECSE-13.directional_reason: A comparable result can change the factual state or time margin transferred; it does not establish uptake, consent or transfer of authority.
ECSE-13.native_component: Physical state results or residual physical time limits actually transferred at a consequential handoff.

ECSE-15.directional_reason: A reference-comparable interval changes which retention condition the same observed performance supports. No skill scale, learning law or performance at an unobserved interval follows.
ECSE-15.native_component: The native retention interval and performance demonstration for the actual class of unexpected event.

ECSE-16.directional_reason: Result-level comparability can alter whether the concrete advice or check is warranted; this is not metrological calibration of trust or an instruction to verify every suggestion.
ECSE-16.native_component: A physical measurement in the advice or capability evidence actually used for reliance and verification.

ECSE-17.directional_reason: A corrected physical reference can change whether advice is erroneous or an intervention helps the concrete outcome, without showing that a behavioral countermeasure generally works.
ECSE-17.native_component: Physical task evidence or timed consequence used to distinguish correct advice, correction and overall performance.

ECSE-18.directional_reason: Reference-comparable event values or durations can change urgency and whether a response fits; they do not supply attention, authority or capacity.
ECSE-18.native_component: Physical event evidence, time to consequence and actual response duration in the alert-to-response path.

ECSE-19.directional_reason: Comparable physical results can distinguish threshold drift or timing errors from real demand changes; lower alert count alone still does not establish benefit.
ECSE-19.native_component: Physical alert thresholds, event timestamps or duration/exposure measures in the continuing alarm review.

ECSE-22.directional_reason: A comparable duration changes the exposure condition under which the observed detection/readiness is credited. It does not measure engagement in physical units.
ECSE-22.native_component: The explicit automated-duration input and subsequent-exception horizon.

ECSE-24.directional_reason: Reference comparability can reveal that apparently conflicting or agreeing observations use incompatible scales; it does not require identical interpretations.
ECSE-24.native_component: Physical observations used as the common factual reference across actors or instruments.

ECSE-25.directional_reason: A shared calibration reference or uncertainty contribution can reveal a common error input in apparently different observations. This bounds informational diversity; it does not stage independent inquiry or create unique observations.
ECSE-25.native_component: The reference identity in documented calibration chains of physical observations claimed to provide different information.

ECSE-26.directional_reason: Reference-corrected values can change the apparent relation or boundary used in diagnosis while leaving the display geometry unchanged.
ECSE-26.native_component: Actual physical constraint/state estimates shown in a constraint-based representation.

ECSE-27.directional_reason: A corrected physical value can change whether the procedure's premise holds; it does not authorize deviation or prove a novel alternative safe.
ECSE-27.native_component: A physically measured procedure premise or deviation actually used to choose procedure, adaptation or escalation.

ECSE-28.directional_reason: A valid reference chain can support or defeat the explanation's specific physical evidence claim; it says nothing about faithful internal reasoning or persuasion.
ECSE-28.native_component: An actual metrological result or chain offered as checkable evidence in the decision-linked explanation.

ECSE-29.directional_reason: Reference changes can alter the factual basis of learned reliance even if interface wording is unchanged; trust repair itself remains an outcome question.
ECSE-29.native_component: A changed calibration, range or physical performance result in evidence of changed capability.

ECSE-30.directional_reason: Comparable state or timing information can change a coordinated adjustment; it cannot create directability rights or an anthropomorphic team relationship.
ECSE-30.native_component: A measured physical partner state, available duration or capacity limit used in actual interdependent coordination.

ECSE-31.directional_reason: Reference-corrected feedback can change which expectation is contradicted by the world, without validating a whole mental-model theory.
ECSE-31.native_component: Physical predicted/observed boundary behavior used to check an operational expectation.

ECSE-32.directional_reason: A result-level correction can change a timeline or observed condition while accounts are unchanged; it does not establish the causal explanation by itself.
ECSE-32.native_component: Physical contemporaneous observations or elapsed event times used to distinguish causal reconstructions.

ECSE-33.directional_reason: A corrected indicator or remaining interval can change whether a proposed degraded service or recovery option is feasible; no physical scale for generic adaptability is claimed.
ECSE-33.native_component: Physical demand/capacity or boundary indicators, including available recovery time, actually used to assess the remaining option.

ECSE-34.directional_reason: Reference-comparable physical burden can change whether added coordination earns its cost; it does not determine all social values or excuse a required protection.
ECSE-34.native_component: Measured physical duration or resource consumption in the actual whole-work cost/outcome comparison.

ECSE-35.directional_reason: Where an artifact supplies an actual physical premise to a fixed consumer, changed reference validity or uncertainty can change the artifact contribution, correction, replacement or limited retention. P003 need not create the consumer to supply this factual input; no retention duty is cancelled.
ECSE-35.native_component: The physical-result validity and reference conditions of an artifact used by an actual fixed consumer.

ECSE-36.directional_reason: A corrected time comparison can change whether an obligation remains actionable or expired; ordinal dependency order is not automatically a physical timing claim.
ECSE-36.native_component: Physical expiry, due time or elapsed delay on an actual pending obligation.

ECSE-37.directional_reason: Reference-comparable values can change whether the alternate path reaches the credited state in time; they do not make shared resources independent.
ECSE-37.native_component: Physical fallback-state observations and complete recovery time for the specified covered failure.

ECSE-38.directional_reason: Reference comparability can distinguish a real discrepancy from inconsistent scales and can expose a shared reference error; it does not make two signatures independent evidence.
ECSE-38.native_component: A physical result or timing comparison used by the additional cross-check.

ECSE-39.directional_reason: A corrected value can change what physical condition the record supports while preserving what the actor believed then; no hindsight certainty or exoneration follows.
ECSE-39.native_component: Physical cues or elapsed timing present in the contemporaneous records being reconstructed.

ECSE-40.directional_reason: Comparable time/resource results can change the feasibility/distribution account without turning organizational pressure into a physical scalar.
ECSE-40.native_component: Physical work duration or resource demand in burdens displaced beyond the focal role.

ECSE-41.directional_reason: Calibration can change a component time/outcome comparison or its ranking while human scores remain fixed; it does not establish total net benefit.
ECSE-41.native_component: Actual task, error-recovery or verification time and physical outcome measures in the joint-performance comparison.

ECSE-42.directional_reason: A referenced component can support a narrower physical inference without calibrating the latent construct or making unlike scales interchangeable.
ECSE-42.native_component: The physical duration or sensor component of a construct-specific multi-measure assessment.

ECSE-43.directional_reason: A corrected reference value or interval can change which physical condition a query sampled or which answer is factually supported; it does not create an SI scale for awareness.
ECSE-43.native_component: A physical reference-state value or sampled time used in administering/scoring a task-specific situation query.

ECSE-45.directional_reason: Calibration can change a concrete model input or validation comparison; it does not complete unselected phases or show that a full CWA program helps.
ECSE-45.native_component: Physical domain constraints or timed task results in an actually selected CWA phase.

ECSE-46.directional_reason: Reference-comparable sensor values can change the displayed constraint relation or outcome comparison while layout is fixed; they do not prove EID superiority.
ECSE-46.native_component: The explicit sensor data feeding the ecological interface and any timed task comparison.

ECSE-47.directional_reason: A comparable interval changes the retention condition supported by the observed behavior; a calibrated duration does not show fewer accidents or transport a training effect.
ECSE-47.native_component: The native training/transfer retention interval and physical performance measures actually used in CRM evaluation.

ECSE-48.directional_reason: Reference-corrected evidence can change whether a particular item is satisfied; it does not attribute a bundle effect to the form or prove consent from completion.
ECSE-48.native_component: A physical check result or time limit actually included among stable actionable checklist/handoff items.

ECSE-49.directional_reason: Calibration can change whether a trigger is met or how transition cost compares; it does not validate a latent trigger construct or select the policy.
ECSE-49.native_component: A physical sensor trigger or actual transition duration in the particular adaptive-allocation policy.

ECSE-50.directional_reason: A corrected sensor result can change the physical evidence entering the inference while leaving construct validity unresolved; it does not authorize the resulting allocation.
ECSE-50.native_component: The physical sensor/time component of the stated sensor/report input to a workload-inference policy.

ECSE-51.directional_reason: A comparable duration can change the administration condition supported by the report; it does not make TLX dimensions natural units or infer safety from the score.
ECSE-51.native_component: The physical retrospective reporting interval or timed task condition under which subjective workload is elicited.

ECSE-53.directional_reason: Reference-corrected performance can change the comparison without restoring the rejected universal allocation rule.
ECSE-53.native_component: Measured physical capability or task time actually used in the bounded human/machine comparison.

ECSE-54.directional_reason: A valid physical result can defeat a false intervention credit while the click is identical; it does not make every human step effective.

record.name: Physical result/reference input to CSS-L3

ESS-001.directional_reason: Correcting the consumed physical result can change the factual exposure or scope input while the normative loss boundary stays fixed. This neither chooses unacceptable losses nor supplies authority; a physical premise can change without altering the value judgment.
ESS-001.native_component: Physical exposure, environment or use information consumed in determining the factual scope of the adopted loss analysis.

ESS-002.directional_reason: Reference-corrected state or exposure values can change which hazardous condition the observation supports; failure-free components remain insufficient evidence of safe state.
ESS-002.native_component: Physical hazardous-state, exposure or boundary indicators in the native loss-linked state model.

ESS-003.directional_reason: A result-level chain can change whether the evidence supports compliance with the concrete physical constraint, without allocating or enforcing the control.
ESS-003.native_component: A physical value or timing result used to verify that an allocated constraint is maintained.

ESS-004.directional_reason: A reference correction can add, remove or change an actual search lead or reopening signal. It does not prove search completeness, enumerate every hazard or identify the entire causal mechanism; the native operational-signal feedback is the consumed partial input.
ESS-004.native_component: An actual physical signal, measured condition or reference failure used as a hazard-search lead or reopening input.

ESS-005.directional_reason: Comparable physical results can change an effect magnitude, detection limit or recovery-delay conclusion used in the failure-effects account; they do not prove complete hazard coverage.
ESS-005.native_component: Physical failure-effect or detection results actually used in the bounded component analysis.

ESS-006.directional_reason: A corrected physical result can change whether the defined event occurred or which timed progression is supported; a reference chain supplies neither event probability nor causal completeness.
ESS-006.native_component: A physical threshold event or timed progression interval actually used to define an event in the causal logic.

ESS-007.directional_reason: Comparable physical values can change whether an observed deviation is genuinely above/below the intended condition; guidewords and workshop completion remain separate.
ESS-007.native_component: Physical process/design-intent values and deviations used in a focused process-deviation inquiry.

ESS-008.directional_reason: Calibration can change whether an action was late, persisted too long or occurred in the hazardous physical context; it does not exhaust unsafe interactions.
ESS-008.native_component: The explicitly required action timing/duration and physical process-state feedback in an unsafe-control scenario.

ESS-009.directional_reason: A referenced measurement can change whether achieved state is supported or must remain unknown; it does not create coverage, an actuator or a response authority.
ESS-009.native_component: Physical state, freshness and latency results on the consequential feedback path.

ESS-010.directional_reason: Reference correction can reveal a state/model discrepancy even if the internal model and mode labels are unchanged; no whole-model validity follows.
ESS-010.native_component: Physical state estimates and transition/update timing supporting the controller's process model.

ESS-011.directional_reason: Reference-comparable times can change a late/expired/overlong action conclusion while the message sequence is identical; logical causal order alone does not require physical time calibration.
ESS-011.native_component: Actual durations, timeouts and timestamps interpreted under the native clock/order assumptions.

ESS-012.directional_reason: A corrected result or changed calibration range can invalidate an interface-assumption claim without breaking the data format.
ESS-012.native_component: A physical range, timing or measurement-reference assumption actually asserted at an integration interface.

ESS-013.directional_reason: A shared reference or common uncertain calibration contribution can expose a common error source in nominally independent channels; it does not quantify that error probability or prove all dependencies covered.
ESS-013.native_component: Documented common reference/calibration contributions or physical shared-resource results in the actual dependence argument.

ESS-014.directional_reason: Comparable channel results can change an apparent disagreement or reveal shared reference error; they do not make redundancy beneficial or independent by themselves.
ESS-014.native_component: Physical channel values, disagreement thresholds or degraded-capability results used in the redundancy arrangement.

ESS-015.directional_reason: Reference differences or a common reference contribution can change whether apparent discrepancies are real, whether findings are distinct, or what factual reconciliation is needed. This enters the native reconciliation of conflicting results without proving causal completeness or method superiority.
ESS-015.native_component: An actual comparison of findings about the same physical result in the selected complementary method portfolio.

ESS-016.directional_reason: A corrected state or duration can change the factual basis for a feasible takeover or handoff, without providing understanding, training or control rights.
ESS-016.native_component: Physical mode/state evidence and the explicitly considered takeover time in the human–automation allocation.

ESS-017.directional_reason: A comparable result can prevent transferring a false physical state or residual margin; it does not transfer mandate or make responsibility legitimate.
ESS-017.native_component: A physical process-state result or remaining time limit actually handed off with a consequential constraint.

ESS-018.directional_reason: The calibration chain can change whether that physical evidence supports the linked claim; document traceability and metrological traceability remain different relations.
ESS-018.native_component: A physical verification result linked semantically from a hazard/constraint to implementation.

ESS-019.directional_reason: A comparable measured component can change an exposure or consequence input while leaving the policy valuation and event probability unresolved.
ESS-019.native_component: A physical consequence/exposure value actually used in the uncertainty-aware risk representation.

ESS-020.directional_reason: Reference-comparable durations can change whether the assumed response margin is credible and thus the relevant control burden; no universal process depth follows.
ESS-020.native_component: Physical propagation, observability latency or recovery duration in the consequence/coupling tailoring decision.

ESS-021.directional_reason: A corrected result can show that exposure or the accepted physical interval is outside the asserted evidence scope; it does not decide acceptability or legal mandate.
ESS-021.native_component: Actual physical exposure, barrier-state values or time limits bounding a residual-risk decision.

ESS-022.directional_reason: Reference correction can change a factual exposure or sacrifice component; it does not establish jurisdiction, good practice or the proportionality judgment.
ESS-022.native_component: A physical exposure, control-effectiveness result or time/resource sacrifice component actually used in the proportionality argument.

ESS-023.directional_reason: A calibrated result can change whether a barrier is available or a test meets its physical criterion; common chains can also bound supposed measurement independence.
ESS-023.native_component: Physical barrier-state, surveillance or proof-test result used to credit a distinct layer.

ESS-024.directional_reason: Reference-comparable results can change whether the actual function evidence meets its criterion; they do not assign an integrity level or certify total safety.
ESS-024.native_component: A physical safety-function, diagnostic or timing result in graded function assurance.

ESS-025.directional_reason: A shared reference or unsupported chain can constrain a claim of independent physical evidence; a valid chain alone does not provide independent challenge.
ESS-025.native_component: Reference identities and uncertainty-bearing chains of physical measurements offered as independently informative evidence.

ESS-026.directional_reason: Its reference chain can support or defeat the physical evidence premise without proving the whole safety argument or its completeness.
ESS-026.native_component: A specific physical measurement result already used as evidence in a live claim–argument–evidence case.

ESS-027.directional_reason: A missing, changed or inadequate chain can constitute a concrete defeater of a physical measurement claim; it does not resolve all objections or confer closure authority.
ESS-027.native_component: A claimed physical result or calibration premise challenged by contrary evidence.

ESS-028.directional_reason: A different calibration state/range can make a nominally matching evidence file inapplicable to the deployed physical result; a hash cannot supply this fact.
ESS-028.native_component: The native explicitly listed calibration, parameter and environment identity of a reused physical result.

ESS-029.directional_reason: Calibration-state change can identify an affected physical claim that cannot be reused unchanged; it does not prove every other claim affected.
ESS-029.native_component: A changed physical measurement component, reference, operating range or affected physical test in impact analysis.

ESS-030.directional_reason: A changed reference or uncertainty can invalidate a current physical evidence premise even without a new incident; no requirement for continuous dashboards follows.
ESS-030.native_component: Physical control-health, telemetry or envelope values whose current validity sustains a live assurance claim.

ESS-031.directional_reason: A chain discrepancy can supply a distinct finding about that physical result; neither a calibration certificate nor assessor count proves independent assessment quality.
ESS-031.native_component: A physical test or measurement claim inside the actual independent-assessment scope.

ESS-032.directional_reason: Reference-comparable observations can change whether the abstraction corresponds to the physical implementation while leaving the theorem valid.
ESS-032.native_component: A physical model-correspondence result used alongside a formal proof of the abstract property.

ESS-033.directional_reason: A corrected or invalidated physical reference can change a feedback-integrity premise; calibration alone cannot rule out adversarial manipulation or grant secure observability.
ESS-033.native_component: Physical control/feedback values or timing used at a safety–security shared interface.

ESS-034.directional_reason: Reference-corrected values or intervals can change whether the signal is timely/discriminating for the actual precursor; no authorized responder is created.
ESS-034.native_component: Physical precursor values, detection latency and full response time in the actionable hazard alarm.

ESS-035.directional_reason: A calibrated state or duration result can defeat the claim that a received stop command achieved containment; actual actuation and confirmation remain separate.
ESS-035.native_component: Actual physical containment state, residual energy/material and containment duration.

ESS-036.directional_reason: A reference correction can change whether continued degraded operation lies inside its actual envelope or time limit; it does not choose between stopping and continuing losses.
ESS-036.native_component: Physical mode-specific envelope values and time spent in degraded operation.

ESS-037.directional_reason: Comparable test results can change whether restoration is supported, without supplying the authorized restart decision.
ESS-037.native_component: Physical constraint/barrier-restoration tests and state observations used for restart.

ESS-038.directional_reason: Reference-comparable exposure or duration can change whether the exceptional operation remains inside its stipulated factual bounds; it does not issue or renew a waiver.
ESS-038.native_component: The explicit physical time/exposure and compensating-control health bounding temporary operation.

ESS-039.directional_reason: A comparable duration can change the exposure denominator or response-delay interpretation while the report count is identical; no event probability or causal benefit is established.
ESS-039.native_component: Physical exposure duration and time-to-triage/action in the actual reporting-and-learning account.

ESS-040.directional_reason: A corrected reference or interval can rule out a factual scenario premise without proving the remaining causal account or stopping all further inquiry.
ESS-040.native_component: Physical event/state and timeline evidence used to discriminate competing causal scenarios.

ESS-041.directional_reason: Reference correction can change whether the expected physical control condition is observed; documentation closure still does not establish causal effectiveness.
ESS-041.native_component: A physical control-performance indicator or verification result used to judge the implemented correction.

ESS-042.directional_reason: Comparable measurements can change whether the indicator crosses its physical threshold or uses a valid exposure denominator; calibration does not validate a causal leading-indicator hypothesis.
ESS-042.native_component: Physical envelope/exposure or barrier-state indicators with a stated decision threshold.

ESS-043.directional_reason: Reference-comparable factual components can change the burden or control-state account without calibrating organizational culture or choosing incentives.
ESS-043.native_component: Physical work duration, available resource or barrier-state information used in a concrete upstream-control tradeoff.

ESS-044.directional_reason: A changed or unsupported calibration chain can change whether the supplied physical evidence applies to the composed system; integrator accountability is not transferred.
ESS-044.native_component: A supplier's physical acceptance, interface-conformance or field-performance result used by the integrator.

ESS-045.directional_reason: Reference correction can change whether the same telemetry supports an in-envelope claim; it does not supply an adaptive policy, permission or control actuator.
ESS-045.native_component: Physical envelope variables, telemetry, exposure or recovery-time results in bounded adaptive operation.

ESS-046.directional_reason: Result-level reference information can supply or defeat a premise of why a direct physical check is decisive. No improvement after the same claim is conclusively settled is required for that premise to be material. An adequate local reference may already suffice; a defective reference can withdraw decisiveness without mandating an expensive new oracle.
ESS-046.native_component: The applicable reference and uncertainty of an existing direct physical discriminator.

ESS-047.directional_reason: Reference correction can change whether the specific physical protection is redundant or still needed; non-use alone remains insufficient evidence.
ESS-047.native_component: Physical effectiveness or burden results used in impact analysis before retiring a control.

ESS-048.directional_reason: Correcting reference validity or uncertainty can change valid use, correction, replacement or restricted retention of that physical evidence. This contribution does not create the consumer, waive a duty or justify automatic disposal.
ESS-048.native_component: A physical premise in a maintained artifact with a fixed real or credible latent consumer and applicable retention duties.

ESS-049.directional_reason: Comparable physical results can change the factual claim that a hazard has been eliminated or exposure reduced; they do not choose the control hierarchy or authorize weaker protection.
ESS-049.native_component: Physical hazard presence, barrier state or exposure reduction used to compare feasible controls.
